course.title: The Agentic Bio Fellowship: Local Agents for Clinical Documentation Hours
course.description: Privacy-first local multi-agent orchestration for clinical documentation workflow. Agents plan; Nextflow executes. Ethics packets stay on campus. 6–8 weeks. Individual ₹1.5L · Team ₹5L.

metadata.description:
A 6–8 week live Fellowship for clinical directors, nurse educators, and radiology/pathology leads. Same technical core as cohort 1. Skin: reclaiming documentation hours — IEC packets and protocol administration, not diagnosis.

Not a medical device. Not clinical advice. Synthetic teaching documents only.
metadata.requirements:
• Owns SOPs or IEC/IRB packets today
  • Docker on a machine you control (or documented blocker + offline stub)
  • No requirement to send identifiable notes to a public LLM API
metadata.goals:
1. Run a local LLM with an explicit document boundary
  2. Ship a Dockerized Python + R image
  3. Treat Nextflow as the execution plane
  4. Index a synthetic IEC packet locally, with human review before any filing
  5. Stop a document loop at a human gate
  6. Deliver one autonomous local pipeline on the synthetic packet

The failure mode

Public model endpoints and identifiable notes, imaging reports, or live IEC packets do not mix. “HIPAA-eligible vendor” is not your DPA. Hospital legal will ask where the text went, who can read the logs, and whether a subprocessor in another country saw a name.

What this track is not

Not diagnosis, triage, or treatment. Documentation workflow only — ethics-committee packets and protocol administration. We do not teach scribes that write into the EHR.

How the live session runs

Ninety minutes on the week’s contract, then the lab is async. Bring a machine you control (or a written blocker plus the offline stub). We will not paste real payloads into a prompt in class.

Pin the image

Clinical IT still pins the runtime rather than “it works on the ward PC.” The image is what you would show to infosec when they ask how document assembly is reproduced.

What to run

Lab folder: labs/02-container-r-python.

docker build -t agenticbio-lab02:local .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/data" -v "$PWD/outputs:/outputs" agenticbio-lab02:local python /opt/lab/summarize.py
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/data" -v "$PWD/outputs:/outputs" agenticbio-lab02:local Rscript /opt/lab/summarize.R

Acceptance

  • Image builds on your machine (amd64 or arm64)
  • outputs/python_summary.txt and outputs/r_summary.txt exist
  • Host python3 / R are not required to produce those files
  • The Dockerfile pins a digest or a major tag you could defend in an audit

Audit trail

The workflow file is the audit trail for document assembly, not a chat log. If an IEC secretariat later asks which checklist version was indexed, the answer is in Nextflow’s report.

What to run

Lab folder: labs/03-nextflow-execution-plane.

nextflow run main.nf -c nextflow.config

Or:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work nextflow/nextflow:24.10.0 nextflow run main.nf

Acceptance

  • results/summary.txt exists after a clean run
  • main.nf has at least two processes wired by a channel
  • You can explain the audit-trail rule in two sentences

Fail, patch, re-run

The agent proposes a fix. A human approves. The container re-runs. Max three iterations, then stop. Do not invent a cloud notebook.

This week’s fixture

Use the broken copy, not the canonical teaching file. Lab: 04-ethics-packet-local-agent.

python3 extract_packet.py --checklist data/broken-iec-checklist.md --cover data/synthetic-protocol-admin.md --out outputs/packet-index-broken.md

Expected: the run fails or the output is obviously wrong because data/broken-iec-checklist.md is malformed on purpose. Write a patched copy under outputs/. Do not rewrite the canonical fixture in data/ without an explicit human yes.

What “self-correcting” is not

Unbounded retries against a production work dir. A bounded loop with a human signature on each patch that changes analysis code or inputs.

What belongs in the image

Interpreters, pinned libraries, the join/parse/retrieve script if it is part of the runtime. Anything a second fellow would need without your $HOME.

What is bind-mounted

Packet fixtures and outputs. Do not bake live IEC packets or identifiable notes into the image. Teaching files are the synthetic checklist and cover.

Network

Image build may use a package mirror. Analysis scripts must not call the network. No cloud protocol copilots. No “just this once” paste into a vendor scribe.

Minimal DSL2

Two processes wired by a channel: count lines, then write a summary. Use -c nextflow.config so the container image is explicit. If the agent cannot see which image tag ran, you do not have an audit trail.

Channels are the contract between processes. Do not reach into another process’s work directory from a side script. That is how “helpful” agents destroy -resume.

What to run

Lab folder: labs/03-nextflow-execution-plane.

nextflow run main.nf -c nextflow.config

Or:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work nextflow/nextflow:24.10.0 nextflow run main.nf

Acceptance

  • results/summary.txt exists after a clean run
  • main.nf has at least two processes wired by a channel
  • You can explain the audit-trail rule in two sentences

Map tools, deny network

On OpenClaw or an equivalent local runtime, map tools to:

  • list_dir
  • read_file
  • run_nextflow
  • run_container

Deny network except optional package mirrors you already trust. Do not give the agent a general bash tool that can upload to an IEC portal.

Implementation

Paste a short architecture note into the week-4 assignment: tools allowed, tools denied, and where the human gate sits. The gate sits before anything that would look like a filing.

Never auto-merge

  • An IEC / IRB portal submit
  • An EHR or PACS write
  • Invented CVs, insurance certificates, or signatures
  • Rewrites of the canonical checklist without a human yes

If the patch would do any of those, the loop ends and a human writes the next ticket. Speed is not a reason to skip the gate.
